newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert, CBR feature on thinning Belgian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert, CBR feature on thinning Belgian bourse.

text.p: The Bel-20 index of leading Belgian shares closed higher on Wednesday, supported by a jump of nearly four percent in cement maker CBR as well as Wall Street's firmer performance, but with Bekaert still weighing.

The index, which suffered a 0.60 percent fall on Tuesday mainly due to a major sell-off in shares of steel cord and wire maker Bekaert, successfully resisted re-entry into the red, closing up 0.67 percent, or 12.36 points, to 1,861.39.
CBR climbed 3.7 percent to 2,810 francs after touching a 2,845 intraday high. Bekaert and CBR together made up about a third of volume in a thinning pre-Christmas market.

Banque Bruxelles Lambert analyst Jean-Marie Caucheteux said, "We have a 'buy' on the stock from 2,380 francs and we have a target price of 3,100. The market is looking for secure stocks with a good story and a good balance sheet. CBR has this."
Bekaert fell 8.45 percent to 18,150 francs, a further drop from yesterday's 13.43 percent plunge.

The stock started its fall after it announced that 1996 earnings would be close to breakeven because of a 1.6 to 1.8 billion franc restructuring programme needed to help it fight increased steel cord competition from eastern Europe.
Some analysts welcomed the project though.
Pascale Weber at KB-Securities said, "the restructuring efforts will lead to lower costs (depreciation and labour)... Bekaert's expansion potential in the fast growing markets remains intact".

Dealers expected trade to stay thin before Christmas but sharp changes in Bekaert's share price and the replacement on Friday of steel firm Cockerill with electronics firm Barco in the Bel-20 index could raise volumes in coming days.
The index is seen between 1,850 and 1,890 before January.

Steel maker Forges de Clabecq, whose 1.5 billion francs rescue plan was rejected by the EU, closed down eight francs at 83. Becase of an excess of sellers it is subjected by the Brussels bourse to a maximum 10-percent markdown each day
